extracted.intended_audience: chemical patent indexers / patent searchers / information specialists working with DWPI/CPI chemical coding
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for assigning and searching DWPI/CPI chemical functional group, miscellaneous descriptor, and carbon-chain codes when indexing or searching patent chemical structures. Covers Parts K, L and M code usage, exceptions, applicability by date, and search-retrieval recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: K8: >N-O- groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Codes in Set K8: are assigned to >N-O- type groups (various >N-O- permutations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If K710 or K720 is applicable to a N-O group, K8: codes are not also assigned. Prior to 1981 a particular group was coded K800 instead of K840; fragments not covered by K800 were further coded using applicable codes. R in examples can be anything. Some K8 types are assigned together with J2 or J3 codes depending on ester/amidic context. Examples and specific K8 assignments are given (K810, K820, K830, K840, K850, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: K9: O-O bonds
rubrics_metrics.description: Set K9: covers -O-O- type groups including -O-O-Y, -O-O-C=U, -O-O-C#U, and -O-OH (excluding groups coded K910) and other -O-O- groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compounds coded K910 are additionally assigned a code for the group resulting from removal of one O atom unless a specific code takes both O atoms into consideration (example: perbenzoic acid coded K910 and J131; persulphonic acid coded K910, K410, K432). Prior to 1981 K999 was only assigned to compounds with two or more -O-O- groups; since 1981 K999 is assigned when any code from Set K9: is applicable more than once to a compound, even if only one -O-O- group is present. Examples provided (K910, K920, K999 and combinations with other codes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Part L scope: elements and applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Codes in Part L: cover combinations of O, S, Se, Te, N and halogen bonded to C atoms; onium and free radical compounds; sugars and residues; and functional groups with more than one atom in the same ring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some general guidelines for Parts H–L and for less-common functional group codes are referenced earlier and not repeated. Heteroatoms bonded to metals are discussed in a separate section (‘Guidelines for Coding Compounds Containing Metals’). Heteroatoms bonded to B, Si, P and As are discussed in a separate section. Element-symbol placeholders used in Part L are defined (T = O,S,Se,Te; U = O,S,Se,Te,N; X = halogen; Y = O,S,Se,Te,N,or halogen; W = any heteroatom). Codes in Part L are generally not applied if two or more adjacent atoms of the functional group are ring members, except for L710 and codes in L8 and L9 (see rules). Where ring-membership exceptions apply, use appropriate L9: code plus the code for the group with only 1 atom (or none) in the ring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quaternary ammonium coding (Subset L72:)
rubrics_metrics.description: The N+ of quaternary ammonium compounds (N+ bonded to four atoms other than H) is coded in Subset L72:. The parent amine is defined as the amine that remains when the simplest substituent on N+ is removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The parent amine receives all applicable codes from Parts H: through L: (thus negating H1 eliminates many documents referring to ammonium compounds). Exceptions: (1) the tertiary amine code H103 is not assigned to ammonium compounds; (2) if N and all substituents are members of the same ring system, the parent amine is not coded. Order of increasing simplicity for substituents: heterocyclic, aromatic, alicyclic, aliphatic. Examples of L721/L722 assignments shown; note when no H1: code is present because parent is not an amine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part L: code-year applicability and subheadings
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise specified, codes are valid from 1963 in Subs M0–M4 (i.e., subheadings applicability by date must be observed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subheadings applicable to Part L codes are indicated per subset; check year applicability when constructing searches (green/blue/black coding-sheet conventions referenced elsewhere in guide).

rubrics_metrics.name: L1: -C#N, -N#C and related groups
rubrics_metrics.description: All groups containing -C#N are assigned the first applicable code in Set L1:. If the group is not fully described by that code, additional codes from Parts K: or L: may be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If group bonded to different carbon types (heterocyclic, aromatic, alicyclic, aliphatic) choose appropriate L14x subclass (L141–L146). Pre-1981 precursor L141 existed. Examples using combinations (e.g., L141 + J271, L130 + K820) are provided. The rule: assign the first applicable code and supplement with additional codes if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: L2: Isocyanate/related >N=C=.. groups and bonding rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Set L2: codes apply to groups such as U=C=N-, U-C(=N-)-U, -N=C=N-, -N=C=S, -N=C=O and other related >N=C- groups (with many subcodes L210–L299).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a group matching L2: is bonded to R–C(=T)– (R not O,S,Se,Te,N,or halogen), assign an L2: code and an additional code from J2: (Ester, Thioester) or J3: (Amide, Thioamide) as applicable; do not assign an L3: code since L3: is for other groups. If one terminal N atom of an L2: group is double-bonded to C, additionally assign L355 (>C=N-). Groups coded L280 or L290 do not receive extra codes to identify which atom “T” represents and are not additionally assigned L650 or L660. Examples and exclusions provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: L3: Other C=N groups — element-bonding limitations and additional coding
rubrics_metrics.description: Set L3: covers other >C=N- type groups. There are specific limitations on what atoms may be bonded to the leftmost C for certain L3 codes and rules on additional coding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Groups containing >C=N+< receive an L3: code and a code from Subset L72: for N+. Groups >C=N–N and >C=N–O are covered by K630 and K840 and are not additionally coded in L3:. Limitations: to be coded L310/L320/L351/L352, the leftmost C may be bonded to halogen but not to O,S,Se,Te,or N; for L340/L355, leftmost C may not be bonded to O,S,Se,Te,N,or halogen; for L350/L353, C may be bonded to O,S,Se,Te,or halogen but not to N. Codes L354 allow any attachments. Additional functional group codes that apply to the smaller functional groups formed by -C(=N)- and -C(=U)- (except L355) are also assigned. Examples provided and note on tautomeric/related cross-coding.

rubrics_metrics.name: L4: Heterocyclic and poly-hetero >C=... groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Set L4: includes a variety of heterocyclic/heteroatom-containing >C= groups with many subcodes (L410–L499) and rules on combinatorial assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Groups coded L410 are additionally assigned all other applicable codes from Set L4: except L431 and L432; if L431 or L432 are applicable they are coded instead of L410. Example: use L410 for N–C(=S)–N–C(=O)– fragment while L431 covers overlapping fragments. Groups with certain structural formulas receive two or more codes from L4: but no codes from L5:. Groups coded L471 do not receive additional codes to identify atom 'T' (L650/L660 not assigned). Examples demonstrate preference/negation (e.g., L410+L420+L431 but not L531).

rubrics_metrics.name: L5: Other groups with >C=O or >C=S — specificity and additional codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Set L5: covers other >C=O and >C=S types (L511–L599) with detailed rules on when these codes are used versus more specific codes and what additional codes are added.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Codes L512–L543 have unspecified C attachments and are not used when all unspecified atoms are O,S,Se,Te,N and/or halogen; L550, L560, and L570 are applicable even when attachments are only those atoms. From 1978, the X atom of L511/L512 is identified by a halogen code from Set C0:. Parent acid corresponding to L511 additionally assigned all applicable functional group codes including L410 if applicable. Groups coded L512, L531, L541, or L542 do not receive additional codes to identify atom 'T'. Groups coded L520 receive additional codes for the T–Y portion (Part K: bond between heteroatoms), the -C(=T)-N< portion (J3: amide/thioamide), and -NO2 as nitro (H3:). L541 receive additional codes from L440–L472 and L511 if applicable. L550 receives additional codes for functional group formed by S, but such groups are not additionally coded as thioesters. Historical/searchability notes: L560 searchable prior to 1981 for certain structures; L570 searchable prior to 1981 only for S bonded solely to C. Valency for S in L570 is additionally coded. Examples illustrate multi-code assignments (e.g., L550+K442+C316).

rubrics_metrics.name: L6: Combined heteroatom–C group coding and exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Set L6 codes (L610–L660) describe groups combining C and heteroatoms (N, S, O, etc.) and set rules for additional/less-specific code assignments and ring membership constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Groups coded L610, L620 or L630 are not additionally assigned less-specific codes L640, L650, or L660. The C atom in definitions of L640/L650/L660 may be a ring member but adjacent heteroatoms may not be members of the same ring. None of L640/L650/L660 are assigned if unspecified attachments of C constitute a multiple bond to a heteroatom. Smaller functional groups formed by N and U in fragments coded L610 and L640 are additionally assigned any applicable codes. If S–C(–T)–N< is present overall as L620, the smaller functional group formed by N is also assigned applicable codes. Groups coded L620 or L650 do not receive an additional code to identify which atom 'T' represents. Hydrates HO–C–OH and HO–C–SH are not coded L650 or L660 but assigned codes for corresponding >C=O or >C=S groups (water removed). Examples illustrate multi-code assignments (L610 with H-type codes, L620 with amine codes, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: L7: Miscellaneous element descriptors — onium, radicals, ions, valencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Subset L7: covers onium ions, free radicals, charged species and valency descriptors (L710, L721–L724, L730–L760, L799 etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valency (L710, L760) is defined by number and type of bonds an atom participates in, not by change (e.g., N+R4 is 4-valent and does not get L760). L740 is not used for metal salts — guidelines for metal salts in Part A notes. The central element in L730/L740/L750/L760 also receives an element code from Part C:. L710 is black on coding sheet but only searchable prior to 1981 if S is bonded solely to C/H; such groups are also coded C216 or C316. S–Y or S=Y bonds present in L710-coded compounds are additionally coded in Part K:. Onium salts not covered by L710. Charge separation formulae are coded with a multiple bond instead of charges (e.g., specific example yields J371 and K532 rather than L7:). Examples include L722 with H141, L750 with C/C codes, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: L8: Sugars and derivatives coding (Subsets L81–L83)
rubrics_metrics.description: Set L8: codes describe cyclic and acyclic sugars and derivatives with two or more asymmetric centres, types of sugar configuration, number of linked sugar units, and type of compound/residue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Codes in L8 describe sugars and residues (L81 type of configuration, L82 number of linked sugar units, L83 type of compound/residue). From 1981 forward, L81 and L83 codes are assigned to all polysaccharides to which V735 (Polysaccharide) applies; polysaccharides of unknown structure are coded L810; polysaccharides do not receive L82 codes. Functional groups present in a sugar residue (e.g., -OH, -CHO) receive additional functional group codes. A sugar containing a free aldehyde or ketone is always searched in the open chain form. Glyceraldehyde, pentaerythritol, cyclitols and similar compounds are not coded in Set L8:. Deoxy-sugars are not assigned the code of the corresponding oxysugar (e.g., deoxymannose coded L817 not L816). L819 indicates presence of one of L811–L818 more than once (searchable since 1981/week 27); L899 indicates presence of two separate sugar residues (searchable prior to 1981/week 27). L83 subcodes detail oxidised, reduced, N-bonded, and other configurations; examples supplied.

rubrics_metrics.name: L9: Groups in rings — ring-membership and tautomer handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Set L9: covers functional group patterns where underlined atoms must be members of the same ring (e.g., -U-C(=U)-U-C(=U)-, >N-C(=O)-N<, quinone structures, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a Set L9 code to be applicable the underlined atoms must be members of the same ring and the atoms not underlined must not be members of the same ring system as the underlined atoms. Except for L951, L952 and L960, codes in L9 include optionally substituted tautomeric forms, but such application to substituted tautomers has not been reliably applied and should be used with care. L951 covers quinone/thioquinone structures (specific atom sets), with additional valency coding for S/Se/Te; extended quinones with substituents on different rings of a fused system are not searchable as L951. L952 covers analogous structures when at least one atom E or E' is other than O,S,Se,Te; functional groups formed by E/E' receive applicable codes; extended quinones not searchable as L952. Historical notes: prior to 1981 diphenyl/triphenyl methane dyes coded differently across CPI sections, but from 1981 coded as carbonium salts in all sections. Examples show negations (e.g., L941 but not L943).

rubrics_metrics.name: Part M scope: miscellaneous descriptors and search codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Part M: covers a broad set of miscellaneous descriptors including bonds/linking groups between rings, carbon chains, type of structure, ring counts/types, role of compound(s), stereochemistry, time-ranging and control codes for DWPI retrieval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part M codes are applicable to a variety of subheadings; the part explains concepts and provides guidance on which subheadings and time ranges each code applies to. The Section introduces symbol definitions (U, V, V', W, W', W'') and notes precursor-code search behavior (precursor codes only searchable between certain years and should be OR'ed with later codes when searching historical ranges).

rubrics_metrics.name: M1: Rules for assigning linking-groups-between-rings codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Set M1: codes are assigned to linking bonds or groups between C atoms of two separate ring systems, and to the types of rings linked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Codes from M1: are only assigned when all of the following are met: (a) the entire linking group must either be a bond or be fully described by one of the codes in Subset M13: or M14:; (b) the linking group must be bonded to C atoms in both rings; (c) no atom in the straight chain between the two rings may itself be a ring member (except for M150 — consult its definition); and (d) the two rings to which the linking group is bonded cannot form part of the same ring system. Definitions: benzene = unfused benzene ring or benzoquinone; aryl = benzene fused to one or more rings; other = ring other than fused/unfused benzene. In most cases the code depends only on direct chain of atoms; other atoms/bond multiplicity do not affect code unless specified. Subsets M13:M14 must describe entire direct line between rings, not just part of it. If no M1 code applies, M1 can be negated (see negation rules). Examples and reference to subheading applicability and years included.

rubrics_metrics.name: M11: Single/double bond ring-link classifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Subset M11: use codes to indicate rings linked by a single or double bond with distinctions by ring types (benzene, aryl, other) — e.g., M111 Benzene–bond–Benzene, M112 Benzene–bond–Aryl, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions for benzene, aryl and other ring types are given in Part M introduction; apply appropriate M11 code according to ring types on each side of the bond. Use M119 (Poly) when multiple instances apply. Examples provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: M12: Rings linked by linking groups (M121–M126)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subset M12: codes describe rings linked by a linking group (non-bond) with distinctions by ring type pairs (benzene->benzene, benzene->aryl, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply M12 code that corresponds to the pair of ring types and linking relationship (M121–M126). Use M129 (Poly) for multiple occurrences. Definitions of ring types as in Part M introduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: M13: Linking groups containing C atom(s) — classification and constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Subset M13: codes classify linking groups that contain carbon atoms (M131–M137) by number/types of carbon atoms and special features (e.g., conjugation, polymethine, azamethine).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Free bonds at either end of group definitions indicate points of attachment to rings. M134 is not assigned to linking groups coded M133, M136, M145, or M146. Double bonds in M134 must be conjugated throughout the bridge (direct line linking rings) and the bridge may be bonded to rings via double bonds. M139 indicates that one or more of codes M131–M137 applies to more than one group of atoms linking different rings (not to the same group linking multiple ring pairs). Examples illustrate combinations and exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: M14: Linking groups containing no C atom(s) — rules and multipliers
rubrics_metrics.description: Subset M14: codes classify linking groups that contain no carbon atoms (M141–M149), such as -O-, -S-, -N-, -N=N-, and repetitive heteroatom chains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Free bonds at either end indicate attachment points. All W atoms in M146 must be the same; for M147 and M148 the W atoms must not all be the same. M149 indicates one or more of M141–M148 applies to more than one set of atoms linking different rings (not the same group linking multiple pairs). Use M149/M139 as multipliers for multiple distinct bridges. Examples demonstrate assignments (M121+M129+M147+M148+M149 etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: M150: Geminal aromatic linking groups — constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: M150 is used for geminal aromatic linking groups R–C–R' where R and R' are aryl ring systems bonded via benzene ring or quinonoid derivative of benzene to the central C atom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The linking C atom may form part of a ring, be multiply bonded to a heteroatom, or be substituted by additional aryl groups. R and R' cannot be part of the same ring system. Apply M150 per its 1963 applicability; examples given where M150 used in combination with other M codes and with or without M139 multipliers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carbon-chain definition for coding (Sets M2 and M3)
rubrics_metrics.description: A carbon chain is an optionally branched, optionally unsaturated aliphatic hydrocarbon group ending with (and including) the C atom(s) bonded to terminating atoms: ring C; chain C multiply bonded to a heteroatom; or any heteroatom (non-C/H). The valency of a carbon chain is defined as the total number of bonds linking the chain to terminating atoms; number of C atoms includes those in branched parts; terminating C atoms are not counted as part of the chain (e.g., CH3–CO2H is a 1-C chain).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide warns that patents often give general or variable carbon-chain information and indexing may be imprecise; overly precise code searches may miss relevant references. Carbon chains of valency 0/1 are coded such that comprehensive retrieval is best achieved by searching general length codes (M210 for 1–6 C, M220 for 7–10 C) rather than very specific length codes. Rule of thumb: 'When in doubt, leave it out.'

rubrics_metrics.name: M2: 0-valent and monovalent carbon chain coding and retrieval guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Set M2 codes describe isolated carbon chains or carbon chains bonded to one terminating atom (M210 general and M211–M216 specific 1–6 C codes; M220 general and M221–M226 specific 7–19+ C codes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the general codes M210 or M220 is always added to the code record when a specific code from M21/M22 is assigned (e.g., propyl chain not multiply bonded receives M210 and M213). Prior to 1981, specific codes in M21/M22 were only assigned if no polyvalent chains present; from 1981 forward, specific codes assigned only if chain length specifically claimed or exemplified. Therefore comprehensive retrieval is best achieved by searching M210 or M220 rather than the more specific chain-length codes. If structure contains both 0/1-valent and polyvalent chains and a user includes a specific chain-length code, place that code in the search statement with codes from 1981/week 27 onward (green codes), while the applicable general code is placed with codes from 1972–1981/week 26 (blue codes). Sets M2 are applicable to multiple subheadings per table; check exceptions (M232/M233/M240 applicability years).

rubrics_metrics.name: M23: Carbon chain branching rules (M231–M233)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subset M23: codes indicate chain branching: M231 straight chain; M232 chain containing secondary branching; M233 chain containing tertiary branching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: M231 has not been used for methyl or ethyl chains since 1981. Carbon chains coded M232 or M233 are not additionally coded M231. For M232/M233 none of the C atoms shown may be multiply bonded to a heteroatom nor be ring members; the free bond must be attached to an atom other than hydrogen (e.g., tert-butyl substituent would be M233). Carbon chains containing C=C or C#C are assigned same code as corresponding hydrogenated chains. Be cautious searching M232/M233 because earlier 'punch codes' were inconsistently assigned prior to 1972. M240 indicates chain bonded to ring C (1963); M250 chain bonded to V or C=V (V defined).

rubrics_metrics.name: M26/M27: Precursor codes for chains bonded to unsaturated systems and heteroatoms (1972–1981 behavior)
rubrics_metrics.description: Codes M260, M270, M350, M360, M370, and M380 are precursor codes only searchable between 1972 and 1981; implement OR’ing with corresponding later codes when searching historical ranges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: M26 subset covers chain bonded to C=U or C#U (M261–M263 distinctions for C=S/C=Se/C=Te, C=O, C=N/C#N). Note tautomeric assignment rule (e.g., CH3–C(=O)–SH coded as tautomer CH3–C(=S)–OH (M261)). M27 subset covers chain bonded to U (S/Se/Te, O, N). Use multipliers M280–M283 to indicate occurrence counts (none, once, twice, three times). Examples show combination codes (M226+M232+M320+M610 etc.).
